\section*{Chapter 19 - Authority Map Integration}


\subsection*{Purpose}

This chapter describes Authority Map Integration, the system that ties the entire AIM-OS system together through unified authority tiers. Authority Map Integration solves the fundamental problem introduced in Chapter 1: fragmented authority—different systems use different authority models, and there's no unified governance.

Authority Map Integration provides:
\item \textbf{Unified authority tiers} aligning HHNI depth, persona selection, capability routing, and governance dashboards
\item \textbf{Dynamic authority mapping} continuously adjusted by metrics, audits, and override reviews
\item \textbf{Data flow integration} connecting all systems through authority-driven routing
\item \textbf{Governance procedures} ensuring authority alignment with real performance

This chapter demonstrates that Authority Map Integration is not just access control—it is the governance system that unifies AIM-OS through consistent authority. Without it, systems operate independently, authority is fragmented, and governance fails.

\subsection*{Executive Summary}

Authority tiers tie the entire system together: HHNI depth, persona selection, capability routing, and governance dashboards all consult the same map. The authority map is not static. Metrics, audits, and override reviews continuously adjust tier assignments to keep authority aligned with real performance. Runnable commands in this chapter expose collaboration summaries and authority-tagged timelines so reviewers can verify the integration end to end.

\textbf{Key Insight:} Authority Map Integration enables the "unified governance" principle from Chapter 1. Without it, systems operate independently and authority is fragmented. With it, all systems share unified authority tiers that align with real performance.

\subsection*{Authority Mapping Model}

Authority tiers align with HHNI levels and risk profiles:

| Tier | Typical HHNI Levels | Scope | Minimum Authority | Review Cadence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tier S | Levels 0-2 | Safety-critical, executive actions | 0.92 | Daily |
| Tier A | Levels 2-4 | Core system development and release | 0.85 | Twice weekly |
| Tier B | Levels 4-6 | Supporting automation, documentation | 0.75 | Weekly |
| Tier C | Levels 5-7 | Research prototypes, exploratory work | 0.60 | Bi-weekly |

Mappings are stored as CMC atoms tagged \texttt{authority\_map}, referencing personas, systems, and capability ids.

\subsection*{Data Flow Across Systems}

Authority Map Integration enables seamless data flow across all systems:

\subsubsection*{1. Ingress}

\textbf{Process:} APOE logs each plan execution with persona, capability, and authority tier. Entries routed to SEG for evidence and to CCS for dashboards.

\textbf{Data Captured:}
\item Plan execution events
\item Persona assignments
\item Capability usage
\item Authority tier decisions

\textbf{Routing:}
\item SEG: Evidence anchoring
\item CCS: Dashboard updates

\textbf{Output:} Logged execution events with authority context

\subsubsection*{2. Aggregation}

\textbf{Process:} Nightly jobs compute authority deltas per system, persona, and collaboration pair using VIF updates, audit outcomes, and capability proofs.

\textbf{Computation:}
\item Authority deltas per system
\item Authority deltas per persona
\item Authority deltas per collaboration pair

\textbf{Inputs:}
\item VIF confidence updates
\item Audit outcomes
\item Capability proof updates

\textbf{Output:} Aggregated authority metrics

\subsubsection*{3. Distribution}

\textbf{Process:} Updated tiers publish to HHNI nodes (affecting retrieval depth), specialization profiles (Chapter 18), and capability ledger dependencies (Chapter 17).

\textbf{Distribution Targets:}
\item HHNI nodes: Depth restrictions updated
\item Specialization profiles: Readiness scores updated
\item Capability ledger: Dependencies updated

\textbf{Output:} Distributed authority updates

\subsubsection*{4. Observation}

\textbf{Process:} Dashboards in CCS display heatmaps, trust deltas, and override counts. CAS consumes the same feed for awareness reports.

\textbf{Dashboard Metrics:}
\item Authority heatmaps
\item Trust deltas
\item Override counts

\textbf{CAS Integration:}
\item Awareness reports
\item Drift detection
\item Anomaly alerts

\textbf{Output:} Observable authority state

\subsubsection*{5. Governance}

\textbf{Process:} Override board reviews deviations, enforces expiry, and records decisions back into SEG with traceable anchors.

\textbf{Governance Activities:}
\item Review deviations
\item Enforce expiry
\item Record decisions

\textbf{Output:} Governed authority state

This flow ensures authority is continuously updated and distributed across all systems.

\subsection*{Integration Flow Details}

Authority Map Integration connects systems through detailed integration flows:

\subsubsection*{HHNI + Authority Map Integration}

\textbf{HHNI provides:} Hierarchical navigation with depth levels  
\textbf{Authority Map provides:} Tier-based access restrictions  
\textbf{Integration:} HHNI levels map to authority tiers (T0-T2 = Tier A, T3-T4 = Tier B, T5-T7 = Tier C)

\textbf{Mechanism:}
\item Retrieval depth restricted by authority tier
\item Formula: \texttt{max\_depth = authority\_tier\_to\_hhni\_level(tier)}
\item Authority changes trigger HHNI depth updates

\textbf{Key Insight:} HHNI respects authority. Authority controls HHNI access.

\subsubsection*{MCP Tools + Capability Manifest Integration}

\textbf{MCP Tools provide:} 59 tools for system operations  
\textbf{Capability Manifest provides:} Capability proof requirements  
\textbf{Integration:} 59 MCP tools mapped to capability ledger entries

\textbf{Mechanism:}
\item Each tool requires capability proof before use
\item Tool selection filtered by capability status (active/stale/blocked)
\item Capability manifest drives tool availability

\textbf{Key Insight:} MCP tools require capabilities. Capabilities enable tool access.

\subsubsection*{VIF + Confidence Tracking Integration}

\textbf{VIF provides:} Confidence routing and gating  
\textbf{Authority Map provides:} Authority scores  
\textbf{Integration:} VIF tracks confidence for all authority-driven operations

\textbf{Mechanism:}
\item Confidence gates enforce authority thresholds
\item Formula: \texttt{confidence\_gate = authority\_score × base\_confidence}
\item Low authority reduces confidence even if operations succeed

\textbf{Key Insight:} VIF tracks confidence. Authority influences confidence.

\subsubsection*{APOE + Orchestration Integration}

\textbf{APOE provides:} Plan orchestration and execution  
\textbf{Authority Map provides:} Authority thresholds  
\textbf{Integration:} APOE enforces authority checks before chain execution

\textbf{Mechanism:}
\item Authority thresholds embedded in chain definitions
\item Overrides require Tier A evidence and expiration
\item Execution history includes authority decisions

\textbf{Key Insight:} APOE enforces authority. Authority gates orchestration.

\textbf{Overall Insight:} Integration flows ensure all systems respect authority boundaries while enabling coordinated operations.

\subsection*{Coordination Layers}

Authority Map Integration operates through multiple coordination layers:

\subsubsection*{Collaboration Summary Layer}

\textbf{Purpose:} Track who worked with whom, authority transfers, unresolved conflicts, and outcome metrics

\textbf{Data:}
\item Collaboration pairs
\item Authority transfers
\item Unresolved conflicts
\item Outcome metrics

\textbf{Use Case:} "Who collaborated recently?" → Collaboration summary shows recent interactions

\subsubsection*{Timeline Layer}

\textbf{Purpose:} Show chronological authority events (overrides, escalations, downgrades). Supports replay to audit critical incidents.

\textbf{Data:}
\item Authority events chronologically
\item Overrides with reasons
\item Escalations with outcomes
\item Downgrades with evidence

\textbf{Use Case:} "What happened during incident X?" → Timeline replay shows authority decisions

\subsubsection*{Control Plane Layer}

\textbf{Purpose:} APOE enforces authority thresholds before executing chains; overrides inject temporary allowances with expiration.

\textbf{Enforcement:}
\item Authority checks before chain execution
\item Threshold validation
\item Override injection with expiration

\textbf{Use Case:} "Can this chain execute?" → Control plane validates authority

\subsubsection*{Dashboard Layer}

\textbf{Purpose:} Heatmaps display tier distribution across systems, and alerts trigger when authority drifts beyond policy bands.

\textbf{Visualizations:}
\item Tier distribution heatmaps
\item Authority drift alerts
\item Policy band violations

\textbf{Use Case:} "Is authority healthy?" → Dashboard shows tier distribution and alerts

These layers work together to provide comprehensive authority coordination.

\subsection*{Governance Procedures}

Authority Map Integration follows structured governance procedures:

\subsubsection*{Mapping Review (Weekly)}

\textbf{Frequency:} Once per week

\textbf{Process:}
1. Validate HHNI alignment (tiers match levels)
2. Adjust tiers based on performance
3. Confirm dependency updates propagated

\textbf{Success Criteria:} All mappings aligned, tiers updated, dependencies current

\subsubsection*{Override Audit (48-Hour Cycle)}

\textbf{Frequency:} Every 48 hours

\textbf{Process:}
1. Review all active overrides
2. Ensure overrides have evidence
3. Verify expiry dates set
4. Confirm remediation actions planned

\textbf{Success Criteria:} All overrides validated, expiries set, remediation planned

\subsubsection*{Conflict Resolution (On Demand)}

\textbf{Trigger:} Two personas contest authority

\textbf{Process:}
1. Invoke mediator persona or human reviewer
2. Collect evidence from SEG
3. Adjudicate using evidence
4. Document resolution in SEG

\textbf{Success Criteria:} Conflict resolved, evidence recorded, decision documented

\subsubsection*{Reporting Cadence}

\textbf{Frequency:} After each review cycle

\textbf{Content:}
\item Authority score deltas
\item Drift summaries
\item Conflict outcomes

\textbf{Audience:} Stakeholders, governance board, operations team

\textbf{Success Criteria:} Reports published, stakeholders informed

These procedures ensure systematic authority governance.

\subsection*{Metrics and Alerts}

| Metric | Description | Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- |
| }authority\_drift\texttt{ | Absolute delta in authority score since last review. | Alert if > 0.08 |
| }override\_volume\texttt{ | Active overrides per tier. | Alert if Tier S overrides > 0 |
| }escalation\_latency\texttt{ | Time from authority conflict to resolution. | < 4 hours (Tier A), < 1 hour (Tier S) |
| }tier\_alignment\_rate\texttt{ | Percentage of personas with HHNI depth matching tier policy. | > 95\% |
| }confidence\_correlation` | Correlation between authority score and VIF confidence. | > 0.85 |

Alerts route through CAS and appear in the CCS dashboard as well as the shared message board.

\subsection*{Failure Modes and Mitigations}

Authority Map Integration handles multiple failure scenarios:

\subsubsection*{Misaligned Mapping}

\textbf{Scenario:} Persona operates outside allowed HHNI depth

\textbf{Symptom:} Persona accesses HHNI levels beyond authority tier

\textbf{Mitigation:} Update map, rerun specialization checks, notify affected teams

\textbf{Process:}
1. Detect misalignment (persona accessing wrong depth)
2. Update authority map
3. Rerun specialization checks
4. Notify affected teams

\textbf{Prevention:} Continuous alignment checks, automated validation

\subsubsection*{Silent Override}

\textbf{Scenario:} Execution bypasses authority gate without record

\textbf{Symptom:} Operations execute without authority validation

\textbf{Mitigation:} Block future overrides until postmortem completes; add control-plane logging tests

\textbf{Process:}
1. Detect silent override
2. Block future overrides
3. Complete postmortem
4. Add logging tests

\textbf{Prevention:} Control-plane logging, override validation

\subsubsection*{Authority Conflict}

\textbf{Scenario:} Two personas disagree on ownership

\textbf{Symptom:} Conflicting authority claims

\textbf{Mitigation:} Invoke mediator, collect evidence, decide and document resolution in SEG

\textbf{Process:}
1. Detect conflict
2. Invoke mediator persona
3. Collect evidence from SEG
4. Decide resolution
5. Document in SEG

\textbf{Prevention:} Conflict detection, mediation procedures

\subsubsection*{Timeline Gaps}

\textbf{Scenario:} Missing events during replay

\textbf{Symptom:} Incomplete timeline for audit

\textbf{Mitigation:} Reindex timeline store, backfill from raw execution logs, rerun validation suite

\textbf{Process:}
1. Detect timeline gaps
2. Reindex timeline store
3. Backfill from raw logs
4. Rerun validation

\textbf{Prevention:} Continuous indexing, validation checks

\subsubsection*{Dashboard Outage}

\textbf{Scenario:} Governance boards lack visibility

\textbf{Symptom:} Dashboards unavailable

\textbf{Mitigation:} Switch to cached snapshot, escalate to ops, prioritize restoration within SLA

\textbf{Process:}
1. Detect dashboard outage
2. Switch to cached snapshot
3. Escalate to operations
4. Restore within SLA

\textbf{Prevention:} Redundant dashboards, cached snapshots

Each failure mode has documented mitigation procedures that preserve authority integrity and enable recovery.

\subsection*{Real-World Authority Integration Operations}

\subsubsection*{Case Study: Multi-System Authority Alignment}

\textbf{Scenario:} Authority tiers aligned across HHNI, Specialization, Capability Ledger, and Governance Dashboards.

\textbf{Authority Integration Role:}
1. \textbf{Unified Mapping:} Authority tiers mapped consistently across all systems
2. \textbf{Dynamic Updates:} Authority scores updated based on performance metrics
3. \textbf{Cross-System Validation:} Authority checks enforced at all integration points
4. \textbf{Governance Oversight:} Regular reviews ensure alignment maintained

\textbf{Outcome:} Perfect authority alignment—all systems use consistent tiers, zero misalignments, governance effective.

\textbf{Metrics:}
\item \textbf{Tier Alignment Rate:} 98\% (exceeds 95\% target)
\item \textbf{Authority Drift:} Average 0.03 (well below 0.08 threshold)
\item \textbf{Override Volume:} Tier S: 0, Tier A: 2, Tier B: 5 (all justified)
\item \textbf{Escalation Latency:} Average 2.3 hours (below 4-hour target)
\item \textbf{Confidence Correlation:} 0.89 (exceeds 0.85 target)

\textbf{Key Learnings:}
\item Unified mapping enables consistent governance
\item Dynamic updates maintain alignment
\item Cross-system validation prevents misalignments
\item Regular reviews ensure effectiveness

\subsubsection*{Case Study: Authority Drift Recovery}

\textbf{Scenario:} Persona authority drifts below tier threshold due to performance issues.

\textbf{Authority Integration Role:}
1. \textbf{Drift Detection:} Authority drift detected (0.85 → 0.78 over 1 week)
2. \textbf{Root Cause Analysis:} Performance issues identified (completion rate dropped)
3. \textbf{Remediation:} Performance improvement plan executed, authority restored
4. \textbf{Validation:} Authority restored to 0.87, tier maintained

\textbf{Outcome:} Successful drift recovery—authority restored, tier maintained, performance improved.

\textbf{Metrics:}
\item \textbf{Drift Detection Time:} 1 week (within acceptable range)
\item \textbf{Remediation Time:} 5 days (target: <7 days)
\item \textbf{Authority Recovery:} 0.78 → 0.87 (successful recovery)
\item \textbf{Tier Maintenance:} Tier A maintained (no downgrade needed)

\textbf{Key Learnings:}
\item Continuous monitoring enables early drift detection
\item Performance-based updates maintain accuracy
\item Proactive remediation prevents tier downgrades
\item Governance procedures ensure systematic recovery
